STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square plate is typically 20-30 cm. The plate looks like a medium-large dinner plate, so I estimate about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: a fork is visible at the top-left edge, but it is only partly in frame and not usable for a reliable count. The plate spans roughly the width of the frame's central area, and the green beans (about 10-12 cm long) lie across roughly two bean lengths of the plate's lower half, which fits a plate about 24-26 cm wide.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square). Plate area ≈ 25² = 625 cm².

- Green beans (cooked, left-centre): a bundle covering ~70 cm², about 1 cm thick on average. Volume ≈ 70 ml × 0.6 ≈ 42 g.
- Flatbread/tortilla-style wrap with grilled vegetables (upper right): ~90 cm² footprint, flat layer about 0.5 cm thick, plus a grilled zucchini and red pepper topping. Wrap ≈ 45 ml × 0.3 (bread) ≈ 14 g; vegetables (zucchini, pepper) ~25 g.
- Fish/chicken fillet (centre-right, flaky white with some sauce): footprint ~60 cm², average thickness ~1 cm. Volume ≈ 60 ml × 1.0 ≈ 60 g. Some cream or sauce adds about 15 g.
- Cooked spinach under the fish (dark leaves beneath, right-lower): ~50 cm² × 0.5 cm ≈ 25 ml × 0.6 ≈ 15 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The fish sits on a bed of cooked greens, already counted. No other hidden base layer is evident. The total is light, consistent with a few components on a large plate.
